text:
maria: FYI customer 2378 on prod is getting inconsistent types from structured output mode. field "amount" sometimes comes back quoted and sometimes as a number — downstream parser fails.

kevin: Can you paste an example response and request id?

maria: request_id=rc_20260316_abc123. Examples below.

maria: ```json
{"order_id":"ord_9","amount":"1234","status":"PAID"}
```

maria: ```json
{"order_id":"ord_10","amount":1234,"status":"PAID"}
```

samira: Are they using json_mode=strict? If strict mode expects types this will fail when model follows examples.

maria: They said json_mode="strict" in SDK v1.2.4. Repro steps: curl to /v1/generate with payload including schema and a few examples.

maria: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n -d '{"model":"redwood-unified-v2","json_mode":"strict","schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"number"}}},"examples":[{"order_id":"ord_9","amount":"1234","status":"PAID"}],"prompt":"..."}'
```

kevin: Can you include raw responses + headers? Also check if there was a model rollout yesterday.

maria: Headers: status 200, content-type: application/json, x-redwood-model: redwood-unified-v2; latency ~620ms.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2378 (assigned to @kevin). :ticket: 

kevin: I'll repro locally. Two hypotheses: 1) model-side schema drift after example/priming changes, or 2) our postprocessing accidentally coerces tokens->strings for some short ints. Samira, can you inspect the runtime batcher conversion for numbers?

samira: On it. Also ask customer whether examples in the prompt include quoted numbers — that often causes model to mimic quotes even when schema expects numbers.

maria: Customer confirms they included "amount": "1234" in a handful of examples but expect numeric amounts.

kevin: That explains mimicry. But we should still return a clear error for type mismatches in strict mode, not a 200 with inconsistent types. Looks like validation currently only errors on unparsable JSON, not semantic type mismatches.

samira: Agreed. Quick patch: add an extra post-validate step to compare parsed JSON types against provided schema and raise schema_mismatch when they differ. I'll open a PR.

kevin: Workaround for customer: set json_mode="relaxed" or change examples to use numeric amounts. Also recommend parser-side coercion for "amount" if immediate fix needed.

maria: Customer says this breaks their billing pipeline — they ingest amounts as integers and downstream charges are wrong. They need ETA on a hotfix.

kevin: I can push a runtime check + reject-with-400 patch within ~3 hours (oncall window permitting). Need infra signoff.

ops-bot: Deploy request queued (deploy/patch-json-validate) — ETA 2h.

support-bot: Notified customer: we suggested workaround, opened incident and will follow up in 2h with status.

maria: Adding note to thread: tag for postmortem if this is a regression after the rollout.

kevin: Thanks, will update here once PR and deploy are scheduled.
